newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends steady, crusher buying noted.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends steady, crusher buying noted.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed little changed as commercial buying and the strength of CBOT soybeans helped to offset hedge selling and profit taking, floor sources said.
Crusher buying was also noted as profitable margins kept the crush at a fairly fast pace.

The market was briefly undermined around midday by talk a threatened port strike in Brazil may be averted. Port operators, however, later confirmed a 72-hour strike at Paranagua will start on March 5.
Western barley futures closed mostly lower, depressed by commercial selling in fairly heavy volume. Commission houses were the best buyers. March ended $1.60 lower at $139.20.
Feed wheat futures closed narrowly mixed as commission house buying offset commercial selling. The current slow pace of farmer selling helped to underpin values.
Flaxseed trade was slow with May finishing $1.00 lower at $355.50. Feed peas and oats were tradeless.
(Values in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats and peas.)
